# MobileFilmLab v0.2.0-beta.4 — Fold5 compatibility & optional balanced JPEGs

**Oppo Find X9 Ultra remains the primary target.** This beta adds capability-driven Galaxy Z Fold5 support after a user reported working capture but poor image quality. There were no sample files, capability report, firmware version or attached handset for calibration; actual Fold5 quality and fold transitions remain pending.

## Natural output, detail and colour

- Samsung SM-F946* compatibility policy: prefer real, normal-mode native JPEG streams around a 12.6MP budget instead of automatically choosing an expensive high-resolution route. Maximum native capture is opt-in within the 55MP safety ceiling; session fallbacks do not jump up in size.
- Optional **Balanced detail + noise** JPEG rendering: conventional ISO-aware, edge-preserving luma/chroma filtering, mild high-contrast tone balancing and restrained low-ISO detail sharpening. No invented detail, forced global colour bias or app-added neural enhancement.
- **Camera original / recipe only stays the default.** The unedited, uncropped Natural/native/no-grain/no-calibration path still preserves the camera JPEG pixel data. Balanced re-encodes and is explicitly not an original mode.
- **Fold5 Natural (Camera2)** is a display alias, not a new proprietary profile. Existing recipe IDs, the full 77-recipe upstream catalogue + three baselines, favourites/custom names and Oppo behaviour are retained.

## HDR / low light

- Freeze the metered manual-bracket baseline and use consistent bounds/physical request keys for all three shots; briefly wait for reported AE settling on compensation-based routes.
- Require real exposure metadata instead of guessing bracket stops. Use IEC sRGB conversion, retain recovered highlight headroom until bounded display mapping, and reject colour as well as luma motion.
- Keep conservative middle-frame fallback for missing metadata, low texture or failed registration. Fusion is still optional, experimental, translation-only and JPEG-domain—not stock-camera parity or guaranteed motion-free HDR.

## Reliability and layout

- Reuse the fusion middle bitmap, use scanline scratch for balanced filtering and skip a full-size identity-grade allocation. These reduce allocation pressure; no handset speed/battery benchmark is claimed.
- Resize-aware, centred portrait controls on a wide inner display; narrow cover/wide inner UI render checks alongside readable scrolling Settings and Pro-slider regressions.
- Genuine untouched sensor DNG and RAW+JPEG remain capability-gated. Balanced affects only the JPEG, never DNG. No video or cloud processing is added.

## Install / try it

Same package `com.mobilefilmlab.camera`, existing signing key, **versionCode 13**. Install over beta.3 without uninstalling. In **Settings → Device & JPEG rendering**, select **Balanced detail + noise**, keep **Device-balanced native capture / Native pixels**, and start with **Camera2 natural**, 1×, Natural look, grain 0 and Auto exposure/WB. Compare original files before enabling experimental fusion.

Automated coverage includes model/capability/native-size policy, persistent preferences, numerical noise/edge/colour/tone checks, native JPEG/HDR/motion fixtures, original-pixel preservation, RAW policy, all existing regression tests and narrow/wide illustrative UI renders. CI additionally runs Android lint and signed APK identity/alignment/certificate checks. None substitutes for handset photographs, sensor/DNG/editor tests or firmware validation. The software is substantially AI-assisted in development; no generative/ML photo enhancement is added by the app, while proprietary ISP/firmware processing remains unknown.

Owner-authorised regular Latest GitHub Release with a beta-qualified version. Superseded release binaries and alternate signed-APK artifacts are withdrawn only after the replacement APK/site are verified; all source tags/history remain. Downloaded/cached copies cannot be revoked.
